t:
Nothing in this or any other Act makes the increases authorized by section 1 (49)-(52), (53) (B) and (C), (54)-(58), (60), (61), (62) (B), (63), (67), (68), and (71) of this Act applicable to—

    (1) an employee or individual not within the definition of “employee” in section 8101(1) (A), (B), or (D) of title 5, United States Code;
 
    (2) a member of the Metropolitan Police or the Fire Department of the District of Columbia who is pensioned or pensionable under sections 521–535 of title 4, District of Columbia Code; or
 
    (3) a member of a uniformed service.

fable.w: This section only limits which employees and individuals the Act's authorized increases apply to, excluding certain non-covered employees, D.C. police and fire members, and uniformed service members. A reader might be drawn to the mention of District of Columbia personnel as outside parties, but they are named only as excluded classes. No one outside the federal government is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue over any federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section defines the scope of applicability for salary increases, excluding certain groups of federal employees (such as uniformed services or specific DC police/fire personnel). It does not involve consultation, coordination, or decision-making input from parties outside the federal government. The actors involved are all within the government structure, and the text merely limits who receives a benefit.
qwen_block.s: Nothing in this or any other Act makes the increases authorized by section 1 (49)-(52), (53) (B) and (C), (54)-(58), (60), (61), (62) (B), (63), (67), (68), and (71) of this Act applicable to— (1) an employee or individual not within the definition of “employee” in section 8101(1) (A), (B), or (D) of title 5, United States Code; (2) a member of the Metropolitan Police or the Fire Department of the District of Columbia who is pensioned or pensionable under sections 521–535 of title 4, District of Columbia Code; or (3) a member of a uniformed service.

opus.w: This provision only limits which people the authorized benefit increases apply to. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, rulemaking, or right to sue. It names groups like D.C. police and fire members, but only to say they are not covered, not to involve them in any federal decision.
opus.s: Nothing in this or any other Act makes the increases authorized by section 1 (49)-(52), (53) (B) and (C), (54)-(58), (60), (61), (62) (B), (63), (67), (68), and (71) of this Act applicable to—
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through.** The section only limits who gets certain benefit increases. It names groups of people: employees outside a statutory definition, D.C. police and fire members, and uniformed service members. That might look like it involves outside parties. It doesn't, because none of these groups consults, comments, sits on an advisory body, or sues over a federal decision. Nothing here involves outside participation.

qwen_chat.w: This section defines the scope of a pay increase by explicitly excluding certain categories of employees (non-federal employees, DC police/fire, uniformed services). It does not require any consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties before the decision is made; the exclusion is statutory and automatic. Therefore, it does not involve participation as defined.
qwen_chat.s: Nothing in this or any other Act makes the increases authorized by section 1 (49)-(52), (53) (B) and (C), (54)-(58), (60), (61), (62) (B), (63), (67), (68), and (71) of this Act applicable to— (1) an employee or individual not within the definition of “employee” in section 8101(1) (A), (B), or (D) of title 5, United States Code; (2) a member of the Metropolitan Police or the Fire Department of the District of Columbia who is pensioned or pensionable under sections 521–535 of title 4, District of Columbia Code; or (3) a member of a uniformed service.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that excluding certain groups (like uniformed services or DC police) from a pay raise involves a decision that affects outside parties, or that the definition of "employee" implies some consultation. However, this section is purely a limitation on the scope of a statutory benefit (pay increase). It does not require the government to consult with anyone, hold a hearing, or coordinate with outside entities before making the decision to exclude these groups. The exclusion is mandated by the statute itself, not the result of a participatory process.
